B3: Your parents wish to organise a house exchange with a family in France for a month. Write an e‐mail in French to the family and include the following details:  Give a brief description of the accommodation you require  Tell them some details about your area  Describe some activities that could interest tourists in Ireland  Say you will travel to France by boat and will bring a car  Say that your family likes cycling and ask if they have bicycles.

hlSelectionNote: Q1a/b/c are alternatives; Q1a and Q1b refer to the Section A Q.1 passage and Q1c to Q.2. Q3 is printed in Irish and English; the English rendering is used and all five e-mail points are required. Q1b real/imaginary is open creative scope, not a finite response pool. No Section B task prints an illustration.

ordinary.B2A: Source discrepancy: the marking scheme introduces this message as one left for Monsieur Latour, a guest at the hotel where you work as a receptionist, while the paper sets it for your friend Martin/Martine in Poitiers. The five points and their scheme answers match. This card keeps the task printed in the paper.

sourceNotes: Higher Q1 tasks are 40 marks (20 Communication + 20 Language); Q2–Q6 tasks are 30 (15 + 15).
The 2022 deferred Higher scheme has a two-page offset: PDF page 13 is printed page 11. Viewer regions use PDF indices; citations distinguish both.
Higher Q3 is printed in Irish and then in English; the card uses the English rendering and its own word-count line.
Higher Q5 and Q6 print their quotations in boxes whose text layer follows the questions below them; the cards use each box's text and the printed ask.
